summary: This page covers wire weld diagnosis for workpiece heat control and weld penetration, including how to correct common weld defects shown in example wire weld diagrams.
text_content:
Wire Weld Diagnosis–Workpiece Heat Control / Weld Penetration

INADEQUATE PENETRATION    PROPER PENETRATION    EXCESS PENETRATION OR BURN-THROUGH

Not hot enough    Ideal heat    Too hot

How to increase workpiece heat and increase penetration:
(to weld THICKER workpieces properly)
a. Increase weld current    c. Use faster wire feed
b. Decrease travel speed    d. Use shorter CTWD

How to reduce workpiece heat and limit penetration:
(to weld THINNER workpieces properly)
e. Decrease weld current    g. Use slower wire feed
f. Increase travel speed    h. Use longer CTWD

Example Wire Weld Diagrams

Good Weld

Voltage Too Low or Wire Feed Too Slow
TO CORRECT: Increase Output Voltage or Increase Wire Feed Speed

Voltage Too High or Wire Feed Too Fast
TO CORRECT: Decrease Output Voltage or Decrease Wire Feed Speed

Travel Speed Too Fast
TO CORRECT: travel slower

Travel Speed Too Slow
TO CORRECT: travel faster

CTWD Too Long or Wrong Polarity
TO CORRECT: Check Polarity and maintain less than 1/2" CTWD

key_facts: Inadequate penetration is caused by not enough heat
Excess penetration or burn-through is caused by too much heat
To increase workpiece heat and penetration: increase weld current, decrease travel speed, use faster wire feed, use shorter CTWD
To reduce workpiece heat and limit penetration: decrease weld current, increase travel speed, use slower wire feed, use longer CTWD
Voltage too low or wire feed too slow results in a convex, poorly penetrated bead
Correction for voltage too low: increase output voltage or increase wire feed speed
Voltage too high or wire feed too fast results in excessive penetration or burn-through with spatter
Correction for voltage too high: decrease output voltage or decrease wire feed speed
Travel speed too fast results in a narrow, shallow bead with inadequate penetration
Correction for travel speed too fast: travel slower
Travel speed too slow results in a wide, deep bead with excess penetration
Correction for travel speed too slow: travel faster
CTWD too long or wrong polarity results in wide bead with heavy spatter and porosity
Correction for CTWD too long or wrong polarity: check polarity and maintain less than 1/2 inch CTWD
Maximum recommended CTWD is less than 1/2 inch (0.5 inches)
Shorter CTWD increases heat input; longer CTWD decreases heat input
Faster wire feed increases heat input; slower wire feed decreases heat input
Lower travel speed increases heat input; higher travel speed decreases heat input
Higher weld current increases penetration; lower weld current decreases penetration
